name: OPUS
aliases: Outcomes Following Vaginal Prolapse Repair and Midurethral Sling
question: Does a prophylactic retropubic midurethral sling reduce postoperative incontinence in women without stress-incontinence symptoms undergoing vaginal prolapse repair?

design.blinding: single-blind; participants, interviewers, and coordinators masked with sham suprapubic incisions

arms.label: Vaginal prolapse repair plus retropubic Gynecare TVT midurethral sling
vaginal prolapse repair plus superficial sham suprapubic incisions

design.population: Women without stress-incontinence symptoms, with a symptomatic vaginal bulge and stage 2 or greater anterior prolapse, planning vaginal prolapse repair at seven clinical sites.
design.locator: Wei 2012, Methods: Study Design, Patient Population, and Study Intervention; Table 2

verdictNote: Both primary endpoints met; bladder injury, UTI, bleeding, and incomplete emptying increased.
takeaway: In stress-continent women undergoing vaginal prolapse repair, adding a retropubic Gynecare TVT sling rather than sham incisions reduced composite urinary incontinence or treatment at 3 months and incontinence at 12 months, with more bladder perforations, urinary infections, bleeding, and incomplete emptying.

reports.label: Randomized 12-month report
reports.citation: Wei JT, Nygaard I, Richter HE, et al. A midurethral sling to reduce incontinence after vaginal prolapse repair. *N Engl J Med.* 2012;366(25):2358-2367. doi:10.1056/NEJMoa1111967
reports.followUp: 12 months after surgery; 327/337 (97.0%) completed follow-up, and 287/337 (85.2%) had evaluable 12-month primary-outcome data

results.endpoint: Urinary incontinence or treatment at 3 months
results.measure: 3-month composite event; risk difference in percentage points, sling minus sham
results.note: Adjusted OR 0.31 (95% CI 0.19-0.50); prespecified nominal alpha 0.0469 after one interim analysis. Missing composite components counted as failures.
results.locator: Table 2; Methods: Study Outcomes and Statistical Analysis

results.measure: 12-month composite event despite any interval treatment; risk difference in percentage points, sling minus sham
results.note: Adjusted OR 0.48 (95% CI 0.30-0.77); separate primary hypothesis tested at alpha 0.05. Published NNT 6.3 (95% CI 3.9-18).
results.locator: Table 2; Results: Twelve-Month Outcomes; Methods: Statistical Analysis

results.endpoint: Positive cough stress test at 3 months
results.measure: Objective stress leakage; risk difference in percentage points, sling minus sham
Symptomatic composite component; risk difference in percentage points, sling minus sham
results.note: Stress, urge, or mixed incontinence symptoms contributed to the primary composite.

harms.label: Bladder perforation during sling placement
harms.note: All perforations were managed intraoperatively without reported long-term consequences.

harms.label: Urinary tract infection during first year
harms.note: Table 4 denominators are participants with available event data.

harms.label: Major bleeding or vascular complication
harms.note: The full-text table rounds 5/164 to 3.0%; the abstract reports 3.1%.

harms.label: Urethrolysis for voiding dysfunction
harms.note: Four sling-arm women underwent surgery for voiding dysfunction in the first year; P=0.06.

harms.label: Mesh erosion or exposure
harms.note: No sling erosion or exposure was observed during one year.

delivery.label: Assigned sling received
delivery.note: Two women assigned to the sling arm did not receive it; all sham-arm women received sham incisions.

delivery.label: Operative technique and planned repair strata
delivery.value: Retropubic Gynecare TVT during vaginal repair versus two superficial 1-cm suprapubic sham incisions; randomization stratified by surgeon and planned colpocleisis, apical suspension, or anterior repair.

delivery.label: Additional urinary-incontinence treatment during first year
delivery.note: Subsequent incontinence treatment was allowed in both arms.

delivery.label: Operative time and blood loss
delivery.value: Mean operative time was 11.4 minutes longer and mean estimated blood loss 24 mL greater in the sling arm.

delivery.label: Outcome ascertainment
delivery.value: 327/337 (97.0%) completed 12-month follow-up; 306/337 (90.8%) had evaluable 3-month and 287/337 (85.2%) evaluable 12-month primary-outcome data.

reports.label: Postoperative SUI risk model
reports.dateLocator: PubMed 24402598: February 2014 issue; exact online day not verified
reports.citation: Jelovsek JE, Chagin K, Brubaker L, et al. A model for predicting the risk of de novo stress urinary incontinence in women undergoing pelvic organ prolapse surgery. *Obstet Gynecol.* 2014;123(2 Pt 1):279-287. doi:10.1097/AOG.0000000000000094
reports.followUp: De novo SUI symptoms through 12 months after prolapse surgery

results.endpoint: De novo SUI prediction after vaginal prolapse surgery
results.measure: Bias-corrected concordance index of seven-predictor model
results.note: Development dataset 457 OPUS participants; concordance index 0.73 (95% CI 0.65-0.80). External validation in 316 CARE participants: 0.62 (95% CI 0.56-0.69).

results.endpoint: Prediction versus clinicians and reduction stress test
results.measure: Area under ROC curve in 32 held-out OPUS participants
results.note: Model AUC 0.72 versus 0.62 for 22 experts and 0.54 for the preoperative reduction stress test; P<0.001 for both model comparisons.

relations.note: CARE tested prophylactic Burch colposuspension during abdominal sacrocolpopexy; OPUS tested a retropubic sling during vaginal prolapse repair.
